name: spoofdpi
desc: Simple and fast anti-censorship tool written in Go
why: A door into how deep packet inspection censors TLS handshakes, and how fragmenting ClientHello defeats it.

brief.what_it_is: spoofdpi is a proxy tool written in Go, described in its README as a simple proxy mainly designed to neutralize the Deep Packet Inspection techniques used by many internet censorship systems. The README does not say what traffic it accepts or what it emits in technical terms. The official homepage returned only page markup with no readable text, so the description rests on the GitHub README. The tool's executable is named spoofdpi.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a response to Deep Packet Inspection, the filtering technique behind many internet censorship systems. The project's stated aim is to neutralize those techniques.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the mechanism. It only calls spoofdpi a proxy tool. The scout note suggests it fragments the TLS ClientHello to defeat DPI, but I did not see that in anything I fetched, so treat it as unconfirmed.
brief.install_notes: The README says official binaries are provided only through GitHub and official package managers. Packaging status is tracked on Repology. I saw no install commands, configuration steps, or first-run instructions in the README.
brief.standout: The project credits two predecessors, Green Tunnel and GoodbyeDPI, as inspirations. It also points readers to DPIBreak, a kernel-based circumvention tool for Linux and Windows, as a related option. The README's tone is informal, with a Discord link that jokes 'If you can 😅'.
brief.status: unknown. The README has a Repology packaging badge, a Discord link, and a GitHub Sponsors link, which suggest active upkeep, and it talks about 'continued project maintenance'. I did not see a last release date or last commit date, because I fetched only the README and not the release or commit pages.
brief.caveats: The README says SpoofDPI is not available on iOS or Android. It warns users not to download it from other sources because they may contain malware. The homepage returned no readable text. The docs path spoofdpi.dev/docs/ returned HTTP 404, so the documentation link may be wrong. I did not check the license.
